lf-diagram.description: A Mermaid-syntax diagram rendered by Pele, with optional comment targets on its named boxes.
lf-diagram.x-instructions:
Write Mermaid source inside the `<pre>`, HTML-escaping & before < and >. Give each diagram an `accTitle` naming its subject and an `accDescr` describing its relationships, for a reader who can't see it. The diagram lays itself out for the width it is drawn at, on a phone as on a desktop: it wraps long labels and turns a left-to-right flowchart top-down where that doesn't fit, so write the direction, labels and spacing that read best with room, with no frontmatter config fitting it to a narrow window. What it can't narrow that far, such as a long row of siblings side by side, keeps its width and scrolls in its box. Give a node or edge that needs its own tone a Mermaid class, naming an edge by its id (`A e1@--> B` then `class e1 added`), and style it in page CSS with theme tokens: a node as `.pele-node.CLASS`, an edge's line as `.pele-edge.CLASS path` (`stroke`) and its arrowhead as `.pele-edge.CLASS .pele-marker` (`fill`), and the edge's label as `.pele-edge-label.CLASS`. Each drawn box carries its Mermaid id as `data-id`, so a page script can answer a click on one by listening on `body` for clicks inside `.pele-node`; the box itself takes no focus, so offer the same details through a control too. Without `parts`, the whole diagram is one comment target; with `parts="all"`, each named box, such as a flowchart node or a sequence participant, is a target of its own. Edges and messages never are.

`page check --render` reports syntax errors and empty drawings; look at each rendered diagram to check it shows the
relationships it should. Without visual access, check the source's labels and edges
against the claims, state those claims in prose or a table beside it, and report the
diagram as unchecked (`references/page-checkpoints.md`, "Pre-handover review").
lf-diagram.x-example:
flowchart TD
  accTitle: Checkout from cart to receipt
  accDescr: The cart reaches a payment decision; a paid order produces a receipt.
  Cart([Cart]) --> Pay{Paid?}
  Pay --> Receipt[(Receipt)]
